We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$\alpha$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.
authors: Chan Youn Weon, Carsten van de Bruck, C. P. Burgess, Jeong Han Kim, Adam Smith

papers.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
papers.abstract: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate numerical comparisons, some protocols reach a given tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. To examine the limits of preparation, we consider critical states that already carry a slow scalar field and exterior charge. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of $O(\varepsilon^4)$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient connects this reserve to the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow tail on the normal side. This limited reserve constrains how quickly the existing field can be removed. For releases that suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge, the preparation time grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$ under horizon regularity and uniform radial control. Charge transport constrains the same covariant scalar flux that produces horizon entropy, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.
authors: Yu Shi, Sheng Long

papers.title: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
papers.abstract: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.
authors: Xingang Chen, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu

papers.title: Exact Mixed-Locality Encodings for Resource-Constrained QAOA
papers.abstract: Higher-order objectives possess many exact Hamiltonian encodings, and these encodings differ in the qubits, penalties, gates, and depth that they require. Representation selection is therefore an algorithmic decision for the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm on resource-constrained hardware. This work develops a pointwise-exact family of representations in which selected higher-order interactions are replaced by shared Rosenberg auxiliaries while the remaining interactions stay native. A sharp single-step penalty condition and a closed form for cubic residuals certify exactness at every stage of such a selective reduction. Within the direct-pair class, a static feasibility theory identifies infinite families of objectives for which a mixed representation meets joint budgets that exclude both the native and the fully reduced endpoint. A separate construction extends this separation to gate and depth limits under a fixed synthesis. Compilation on 12-qubit line, ring, and grid targets finds certified mixed-only regions for 23 of 30 weighted maximum three-satisfiability instances, all 30 constructed instances, and 2 of 30 cubic spin-glass instances under the stated class and penalty rule. A separate routing experiment retains 52.9% of mixed-only budget points across five seeds within fixed candidate sets. In noiseless depth-one evaluation, the native encoding attains the best mean objective under the tested protocols, and the joint resource-and-quality test finds no mixed-only success at the primary budget. Resource feasibility is thus a sound reason to select a mixed encoding, whereas solution quality requires a separate assessment.
authors: Jingcong Liu, Yiding Su, Ruojun Zhang, Hafiz Muhammad Waseem, Bo Chen, Carsten Maple

papers.title: Spin Structure Factor of the classical Ising Model on the Centered Pyrochlore Lattice
papers.abstract: We present the spin structure factor of the Ising model on the centered pyrochlore lattice. Generalizing Henley's method [Phys. Rev. B 71, 014424] to the case of inequivalent center and vertex spins, we obtain spin correlation functions that are in excellent agreement with Monte Carlo results and can capture sharp and broadened pinch points, also at finite temperature. Our approach can be extended to other centered lattice structures in classical frustrated magnetism.
authors: L. Xu, T. Krei{\ss}el, N. Davier, L. D. C. Jaubert, L. Pollet

papers.title: Critical excited states in quantum metrology
papers.abstract: We investigate criticality-enhanced sensing near ground- and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a strongly coupled qubit-boson system. Accounting for finite-size effects, we design driving protocols that exploit diverging susceptibilities to enhance signal-to-noise ratios in parameter estimation using experimentally relevant generators. We show that the excited-state criticality provides a metrological advantage through single-mode bosonic squeezing in regimes that circumvent the 'death of adiabaticity', limiting conventional critical quantum metrology with ground-state criticality.
authors: Marek Kucha\v{r}, Michal Macek

papers.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.
authors: Wu-yen Chuang, Yi-Jing Tseng

papers.title: Subwavelength registration of skull-compensating acoustic holograms via nonlinear parametric array feedback
papers.abstract: Realizing the potential of optimized acoustic holograms for applications like transcranial ultrasound requires sub-wavelength alignment accuracy (less than 1.5 mm at 1 MHz), which is difficult to achieve with current non-MRI optical neuro-navigation methods. To address the critical challenge of alignment, we leverage the parametric array (PA) signal as an alignment surrogate, a highly penetrative, low-frequency difference wave generated by the nonlinear mixing of two primary high-frequency beams. Simulations show that a misaligned skull-compensating lens increases the primary acoustic energy within the skull bone (volumetric energy trapping), which strengthens the nonlinear source of the PA signal. We also tested whether shear-mode conversion in bone contributes: 2D elastic simulations showed only a small (3-5%) increase in shear-type motion with misalignment, and the transmitted ex vivo bursts did not lengthen as a shear path would require. Pseudo-sound and microbubble artifacts were examined and found unlikely to explain the signal, consistent with the PA signal arising from the intrinsic nonlinearity of the bone. Minimizing this PA signal yields a noninvasive real-time feedback mechanism that achieves sub-wavelength alignment accuracy, outperforming standard neuronavigation. Our findings present a robust framework that supports the design of simple, economical, and high-performance transcranial ultrasound systems for high-precision neuro-interventions.
authors: Pradosh Pritam Dash, Costas D. Arvanitis

papers.title: Large deviations of spatial moments of the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti lattice gas following a localized energy release
papers.abstract: We study the long-time statistics of spatial moments of the time-dependent energy distribution in a one-dimensional Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti model following an instantaneous release of energy on a single lattice site. The moments are $M_n(T)=\sum_i x_i^n u_i(T)$, where $u_i(T)$ is the energy at site $i$ at the observation time $T$. Employing macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT), we calculate the variance of $M_n$ for every positive integer $n$ and determine the non-Gaussian distribution tails for the representative cases $n=1$ and $2$. For the first moment, we establish an exact duality, within MFT, to integrated-current statistics for a deterministic flat initial density. For both $n=1$ and $n=2$, the large-moment tails are dominated by a single adiabatically evolving doublon: a rapidly propagating pair of narrow solitary pulses of the energy density and of the gradient of the conjugate field. The small-second-moment tail is associated with concentration of the energy near the origin at time $T$. Comparing single- and two-doublon histories, we predict a dynamical phase transition at a critical value of $M_2$ at which the optimal path breaks reflection symmetry $x\to -x$. Numerical solutions obtained by direct minimization of the MFT action establish the second-order character of this transition and support our analytical predictions. Finally, we extend calculations of the large- and small-moment tails to arbitrary $n$ and numerically find a transition of the same type for $n=4$.
authors: Timo Schorlepp, Baruch Meerson, Pavel Sasorov

papers.title: Quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields
papers.abstract: The time evolution of the probability distribution for classical fields can be described by the quantum formalism. For free classical fields the free quantum field theory arises as a subsystem. Different probability distributions for classical fields correspond to the classical thermal equilibrium with the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence or the quantum thermal equilibrium with the Planck spectrum. The selection of the Rayleigh-Jeans or Planck spectrum is not a question of fundamental concepts. It becomes an issue of dynamical selection once interactions are present. We compare the momentum dependence of the classical energy and field correlations for the classical and quantum equilibrium. This permits to decide which equilibrium is selected as a result of asymptotic dynamics by numerical simulations of the probabilistic classical fields including interactions. For free probabilistic classical fields we construct a general ``classical-quantum map'' between the classical probability distribution and the density matrix of the quantum field theory.
authors: C. Wetterich

papers.title: Radiative stability of species-separated Kaluza--Klein spectra in warped geometry
papers.abstract: Species-dependent fifth-direction lightcones, generated by scalar-gradient operators, can separate gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein (KK) scales in a warped extra dimension, as recently shown by Randall and Riojas. In this work, we study whether this separation survives quantum corrections. Quark loops can only move the gluon speed within the interval spanned by the bare speeds. Gluon exchange pulls the quark speed toward the gluon speed, with a one-loop coefficient strongly enhanced by fifth-component exchange when the gluon is the slow species. We set the size of this effect using the strong-coupling estimates for a light-gluon benchmark, where a $5.5$~TeV gluon sits below quark partners at $10.74$~TeV. Within the effective theory, the Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes then correct the quark speed at order one. That correction is several times larger than the mass ordering can absorb, so the light-gluon ordering has no perturbative protection. The reverse benchmark, with slow quarks and a heavy gluon, keeps its ordering roughly ten times more robust.
authors: M. A. Anacleto, F. A. Brito, E. Passos, Joao R. L. Santos, J. A. V. Campos, I. E. L. M. Santana

papers.title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
papers.abstract: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, $^{232}$ThF$^+$. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of $^{232}$ThF$^+$, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.
authors: Jinyue Jiang, Kenji Shu, Huaxu Dan, Xing Fan

papers.title: Counting eigenvalues below the lowest Landau level Robin Dirichlet boundary conditions in an annulus
papers.abstract: We study a charged quantum particle confined to an annulus and subject to a strong uniform magnetic field. A Dirichlet condition is imposed on the inner boundary and a Robin condition on the outer boundary. We are interested in the number of bound states whose energy lies below the lowest Landau level, the threshold set by the magnetic field in the whole plane. In the semiclassical regime, we derive an asymptotic formula for this number. It shows how the count depends on the geometry of the annulus, through the length and curvature of the outer boundary, and on the strength of the Robin parameter. We treat both the repulsive and the attractive cases of the Robin condition and describe how the attractive case changes the boundary behavior that produces these low-lying states. The proof reduces the problem to an effective one-dimensional model near the outer boundary and relies on separation of variables in angular momentum.
authors: Marwa Nasrallah, Iman Almoustafa

papers.title: Harmonic superspace and Kaluza-Klein reduction
papers.abstract: We extend the Kaluza-Klein reduction procedure to the framework of harmonic superspace and apply it to the construction of off-shell superfield formulations of supersymmetric gauge multiplets. The reduction is implemented by a deformation of the harmonic derivatives by mass terms, while ensuring that manifest off-shell supersymmetry and Grassmann analyticity are preserved at all stages. As a first application, we reduce the free \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Maxwell theory and obtain an off-shell superfield description of the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive vector supermultiplet. The resulting formulation naturally incorporates an analytic St\"uckelberg-type gauge symmetry. We then reduce linearized \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Poincar\'e supergravity and derive the unconstrained harmonic-superspace action for the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive supergravity multiplet. The technical simplicity of the procedure stems from the structure of gauge theories in harmonic superspace, where the gauge symmetry is naturally encoded in analytic prepotentials and harmonic derivatives. The approach presented in this paper opens a direct route to gauge-invariant off-shell superfield formulations of massive higher-spin $4D,\mathcal{N}=2$ BPS multiplets. Furthermore, the resulting theories can be reformulated in $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ superspace, opening the way to gauge-invariant off-shell descriptions of $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ massive higher-spin theories.
authors: Nikita Zaigraev

papers.title: On Multi-Constrained Path Finding utilizing Grover Search and Decoded Quantum Interferometry
papers.abstract: Finding a path whose totals under several additive metrics all fall inside prescribed ranges is weakly NP-complete. We ask what two quantum algorithms can do for it, against strong classical baselines. For directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) we give a Grover search whose state preparation builds the uniform superposition over all source-to-destination paths with one qubit per arc and no ancilla. We prove it correct, give its exact gate count, and show that measured strings form an error- detecting code whose distance is a girth-like graph parameter. We complete the oracle and count its gates: one search on our largest instance, 136 arc qubits and 262,144 paths, needs about 4.4 x 10^5 Toffoli gates, while classical dynamic programming decides the same instance with 18,754 labels. Grover search needs O(sqrt(N/M)) oracle calls for M good paths among N . Classical meet-in-the-middle matches this exponent in the worst case, and known quantum algorithms with quantum memory beat it. For a staged fabric with node-independent linear weights, maximizing the number of satisfied metrics is max-LINSAT, and with power- of-index weights it is Optimal Polynomial Intersection, where no known polynomial-time classical algorithm matches decoded quantum interferometry (DQI). We verify this translation in simulation and run two small binary instances on IBM Heron processors, which keep 67 % and 15 % of the ideal gain over uniform sampling.
authors: Dmitrii Chemodanov

papers.title: How to find regular black-hole islands in the swamp
papers.abstract: An infinite tower of higher-curvature corrections is expected to lead to regular black-hole solutions. We assume that this regular behavior does not abruptly arise, but gradually builds up with each successive order of the effective field theory of gravity. In addition, we assume that the effective field theory comes with a single scale of singularity-resolving new physics. We translate this assumption into a monotonicity requirement for deviations of the metric functions from a Schwarzschild black hole. Under these assumptions, conditions can be formulated which trace the increase of ``less singular'' black-hole behavior on and outside of the black-hole horizon within the regime of validity of the effective field theory. These conditions constrain the effective field theory coefficients. To exemplify this construction, we motivate five specific conditions and find a corresponding island of black hole regularity conditions at order eight in the effective field theory. We also explore whether string theory as well as asymptotically safe gravity lie on this island.
authors: Astrid Eichhorn, Pedro G. S. Fernandes, Verena Koeder

papers.title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.
authors: Alessandro Arsie, Fabricio Valencia

papers.title: Heterogeneous ice nucleation with TIP4P/Ice: the role of lattice mismatch
papers.abstract: Ice formation, a crucial phase transition for life on Earth, mainly occurs through heterogeneous nucleation on a solid substrate. Despite the importance of this phenomenon, the correlation between the structure of the substrate and its ability to induce ice nucleation remains poorly understood. In this work, we use molecular dynamics simulations with an atomistic model of water to investigate how the lattice mismatch affects the ability of the substrate to nucleate ice. To unambiguously quantify the mismatch, we use substrates with a stretched ice structure. We put the substrate in contact with supercooled water and determine the temperature at which ice spontaneously nucleates during the course of the simulations. We find that the nucleation temperature decreases by $\sim$ 5-6 K for each percent by which the substrate lattice is stretched relative to that of ice. This trend is similar to that previously obtained with a coarse-grained water model [Camarillo et al., J. Chem. Phys. 160, 134505 (2024)]. \textcolor{black}{The substrate induces a fluctuating network of subcritical ice-like clusters, from which a spherical-cap-shaped supercritical nucleus eventually emerges stochastically.} Using Classical Nucleation Theory, combine previously reported homogeneous nucleation rates with heterogeneous nucleation rates computed in this work to estimate key heterogeneous nucleation parameters, including the nucleation barrier, the kinetic pre-factor, and the contact angle. The latter is consistent with a microscopic visualization of nucleation trajectories, supporting the applicability of Classical Nucleation Theory to describe a microscopic phenomenon such as heterogeneous ice nucleation.
authors: M. Camarillo, J. Oller-Iscar, M. M. Conde, J. Ram\'irez, S. Blazquez, E. Sanz

papers.title: Integrable Singularity Black Holes without Inner Horizons in Asymptotically Safe Inspired Gravity and NFW Dark Matter Effects
papers.abstract: We investigate an alternative ultraviolet (UV) structure for Renormalization Group improved (RG) black holes within a phenomenological framework inspired by asymptotically safe gravity. In several regular RG constructions, regularity at the origin is associated with a dS core and an additional inner horizon, raising issues of spacetime predictability and possible mass inflation instabilities. Motivated by this problem, we relate the RG scale to the radially weighted effective quantum gravitational source entering the volume integrand of the quantum corrected Ricci scalar. This prescription yields a Bessel type running Newton coupling with $G_I(r)\sim r$ in the UV, rather than the usual $G(r)\sim r^3$ behavior, and supports an integrable central singularity. The inner branch is matched through the Israel Darmois conditions to an exterior RG solution with $G_{II}\to G_0$ in the infrared, where $G_0$ is the Newton constant. Within the numerical range investigated, the resulting geometry has a single event horizon and no additional inner horizon. We then incorporate an NFW dark matter distribution coupled to the same running coupling. Since $\rho_{\rm NFW}\sim r^{-1}$ while $G_I(r)\sim r$ near the origin, the effective matter contribution entering the field equations remains finite, producing a cored effective behavior without modifying the NFW profile by hand. The gravitational decoupling algorithm keeps the quantum gravitational and dark matter sectors separately conserved within the same geometry. For the configurations considered, the NFW sector shifts the event horizon while preserving the single horizon structure. Thus, the same running coupling governs both the integrable UV black hole geometry and the softening of the central gravitational response of the NFW source.
authors: Milko Estrada

papers.title: Enhanced Entanglement Gate Fidelity via Correlated and Synchronized Atom Motion
papers.abstract: Engineered collective dissipation can correlate and even synchronize the motion of quantum systems. We show that such motional correlations can suppress motion-induced errors in two-qubit controlled-phase gates based on the Rydberg blockade in neutral-atom tweezer arrays. To leading order in the Lamb-Dicke parameter, the motional contribution to the gate infidelity is determined solely by the two-atom motional occupations and correlations, and is independent of the gate protocol. We illustrate this result for correlated thermal states and synchronized quantum van der Pol oscillators. In each case, motional correlations reduce the gate infidelity relative to independent thermal atoms at finite temperature. Our results establish atomic-motion correlations as a resource for high-fidelity neutral-atom gates and may also find applications in analog quantum simulators.
authors: Christopher W. W\"achtler, Frederic Hummel

papers.title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
papers.abstract: We compute the point symmetry pseudogroup of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation using both the direct and the algebraic methods. We also revisit the classical Lie symmetry analysis of this model in detail, concentrating on hidden infinitesimal and hidden point symmetries. Additionally, we re-examine the symmetry properties of each codimension-one reduced model and determine their point symmetry pseudogroups.
authors: Yevhenii Yu. Chapovskyi, Serhii D. Koval

papers.title: The three-loop QCD helicity amplitudes for $V$+jet production at hadron colliders in full color
papers.abstract: We compute the three-loop Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) corrections to the production of a vector boson $V=Z,W^\pm,\gamma^*$ and a jet in quark-antiquark annihilation and its kinematic crossings, retaining full dependence on the number of colors. By expressing the infrared-finite remainders in terms of a small set of rational and special functions, we find that the amplitudes live in a strongly restricted function space, compared to the full space of the related Feynman integrals. We provide fast and reliable evaluation in all kinematic regions using numerical transport.
authors: Thomas Gehrmann, Petr Jakub\v{c}\'{i}k, Andreas von Manteuffel, Cesare Carlo Mella, Lorenzo Tancredi

papers.title: k-partite quantum homomorphisms
papers.abstract: $k$-partite XOR games and linear binary constraint system (BCS) games arise from systems of linear equations over $\mathbb{Z}_2$, providing distinct quantum relaxations of the same classical constraint satisfaction problem (CSP). Linear BCS games have been generalised to synchronous homomorphism games on arbitrary relational structures, with compositional semantics provided by the quantum monad. We introduce $k$-partite homomorphism games, extending $k$-XOR games from linear systems to arbitrary relational structures. This yields a framework for studying multipartite quantum CSPs and quantum homomorphisms. We characterise perfect strategies in both the tensor-product and commuting-operator models as Kleisli morphisms of suitable state-dependent graded quantum monads on a category of $k$-partite relational structures. We then study quantum advantage in the pseudotelepathic sense: the existence of a perfect quantum strategy without a perfect classical strategy. We show that synchronous and $k$-partite quantum advantage are incomparable at the level of CSP instances. The GHZ instance admits three-player quantum advantage but no synchronous commuting-operator advantage, whereas the magic-square instance admits synchronous quantum advantage but no $k$-partite commuting-operator advantage for any number of players or proper colouring. We also exhibit an explicit six-element template whose CSP is NP-complete and admits two-player quantum advantage. Finally, we prove that no bounded-width CSP template admits $k$-partite quantum advantage, even in the commuting-operator model.
authors: Amin Karamlou

papers.title: Potts Order Preempts Emergence of 2-Form U(1) Spin Liquidity in Three-Dimensional Spin Vorticity Models
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin vorticity models (SVMs) have been proposed to realize an exotic 2-form U(1) classical spin liquid (CSL), characterized by a zero-curl constraint, string excitations, and deconfined fluctuating membranes. A previous numerical study [PRB 111, 064417 (2025)] uncovered a puzzle in the pyrochlore lattice SVM: despite exhibiting pinch points characteristic of a U(1) spin liquid, it also develops weak all-in--all-out (AIAO) order. Here, we show that the emergence of the 2-form CSL in 3D SVMs is preempted by an intrinsic instability towards entropy-driven height locking. We establish this by resolving the ground state constraints using a height mapping, which we further relate to a 3-state Potts antiferromagnet. This identifies the pyrochlore's weak AIAO order as permutationally symmetric sublattice (PSS) order, albeit with an exceptionally weak locking strength. We extend the SVM to lattices of corner-sharing octahedra and cubes, where we identify the alternative broken-sublattice-symmetry (BSS) order, a hidden order without magnetic Bragg peaks coexisting with collective paramagnetism. All three models undergo a 3D Ising transition consistent with a symmetry-allowed locking potential in the coarse-grained height theory. The spin liquid persists over intermediate length and temperature scales, but a critical Coulomb ground state ensemble fails to materialize, its correlations cut off by the finite locking length. These findings illustrate how microscopic constraints can determine the ultimate stability of emergent gauge theories in frustrated spin systems.
authors: Michael D. Burke, Mohid U. Farooqi, Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Michel J. P. Gingras

papers.title: Universal Theory of Strange and Bad Metals from Spatially Random Interactions with Underdamped Quantum-Critical Bosons
papers.abstract: One of the most important challenges in condensed matter physics is understanding the macroscopic properties of strange metals, particularly why their resistivity remains linear in temperature over several decades. We propose that a (2+1)d theory of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum-critical bosons through a spatially disordered interaction provides this long-sought-after theoretical explanation. The key novelty of our work is to establish the appropriate separation of scales so that the bosons are underdamped. Using this framework, we obtain two distinct forms for the fermionic self-energy: a conformal-limit solution, $\Sigma\sim\sqrt{\omega}$, and a marginal Fermi-liquid solution, $\Sigma\sim\omega\log(1/\omega)$, corresponding to regimes above and below the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, respectively. These solutions produce Planckian scattering, exhibit exact $T$-linear resistivity, $\omega/T$ scaling in the optical conductivity, as well as $\sim T\log(1/T)$ heat capacity at low temperatures. Moreover, our theory naturally unifies strange- and bad-metal phenomena within a single framework, suggesting that we are now approaching a new epoch in understanding the physics of strongly correlated matter.
authors: Aaron Kleger, Rufus Boyack

papers.title: Swing Surfaces in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in the flat limit of AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, and clarify the relation between Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and the swing surfaces proposed for flat-space holography. We show that the ordinary RT formula does not admit a well-defined flat-space limit and connect this to subtleties of the state-operator map in the flat limit. We then construct an AdS$_3$ uplift of the swing prescription and develop its corresponding information-theoretic interpretation through two complementary approaches. First, we show that the swing surface length computes the mutual information between suitably chosen nearly null boundary intervals in a special class of pure CFT states. The gravity interpretation of this result involves scattering processes which take place deep inside of the AdS$_3$ bulk. Second, we reduce the problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation for swing surfaces to the more general problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation of black hole inner horizons in holography.
authors: Jacqueline Caminiti, Sabrina Pasterski

papers.title: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic characterization of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions with a combination of crystalline and finite unitary internal symmetry. We construct anomaly indices of symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. For generalized crystalline symmetries combining permutations of onsite Hilbert spaces with quantum cellular automata, anomaly indices take values in $H^3(B\widetilde \Gamma,U(1)_r)$ and $H^4(B\widetilde \Gamma,U(1)_r)$ respectively, where $\widetilde \Gamma$ is the total group of crystalline and internal symmetries, and the coefficient twist $r$ accounts for spatial orientation reversal. When crystalline symmetries act solely by permuting onsite Hilbert spaces, the anomaly classes restrict trivially to the spatial subgroup. These results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies at the microscopic level, without assuming a continuum description or emergent Lorentz invariance. We prove that a nontrivial total anomaly index obstructs any symmetric invertible phase. The framework incorporates modulated symmetries where spatial symmetries permute internal symmetries. Our results reproduce LSM and SPT--LSM constraints, with the latter illustrating how spectral-sequence differentials can trivialize candidate LSM anomaly indices.
authors: Ching-Yu Yao, Ryohei Kobayashi

papers.title: Learning Quantum Hamiltonians from the Dynamical Structure Factor
papers.abstract: Identifying the microscopic interactions governing a quantum system is essential for developing predictive theories of materials and validating quantum technologies. Despite considerable progress, learning Hamiltonians from realistic experimental data remains a challenge. Motivated by neutron scattering and quantum simulations, we study the problem of learning a quantum Hamiltonian from the dynamical structure factor (DSF), which captures two-point correlation data in quantum magnets. We show that the DSF encodes sufficient information to efficiently reconstruct broad classes of quantum Hamiltonians. Our approach exploits simple relations between low-order spectral moments of the DSF and microscopic couplings, giving rise to three complementary Hamiltonian tomography protocols based on the high-temperature expansion, strong-field polarization, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, respectively. The framework we introduce establishes practical and robust Hamiltonian learning from common experimental data, with potentially immediate application to neutron scattering experiments.
authors: Nisarga Paul, Thomas Schuster, Jason Alicea

papers.title: $\alpha'^2$-corrections to the bosonic string from an action-level double copy map
papers.abstract: The low-energy effective action of the bosonic string contains higher-derivative corrections of the form Riem$^2$ and Riem$^3$ to the Einstein--Hilbert action, together with the associated Kalb--Ramond couplings. We construct an action-level double copy description of these corrections up to cubic order in the fields. Two ingredients are required: a higher-derivative gauge-theory Lagrangian, which up to field redefinitions is controlled by a single $F^3$ coupling, and a deformation of the color-to-kinematics replacement of the structure constants by the corresponding three-momentum tensor. We show that no higher-derivative gauge-theory operator can produce the Riem$^3$ vertex with the standard replacement rule, and that the matching conditions for the gauge-theory coupling and the deformation of the map admit a unique solution, a double root, which renders the cubic action left--right symmetric, of the form $(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)\otimes(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)$. Without further input, the resulting map reproduces the cubic $\mathrm{Riem}\,H^2$ coupling of the bosonic string at order $\alpha'$, the absence of six-derivative cubic Kalb--Ramond couplings at order $\alpha'^2$, and the absence of interactions odd in the Kalb--Ramond field. The comparison is performed in transverse-traceless gauge, up to field redefinitions.
authors: Eric Lescano, Agustina Pereyra Grau, Jes\'us A. Rodr\'iguez

papers.title: Cosmological correlators and kinematic flow on complex Hartle-Hawking saddles
papers.abstract: The Lorentzian gravitational path integral over homogeneous and isotropic metrics in a closed universe with positive cosmological constant is dominated by complex saddle points, such as the Hartle-Hawking saddles. We ask how to compute cosmological correlators on such complex backgrounds, and how they respond to the shifts of the kinematic variables---the kinematic flow---without tracking the bulk time evolution explicitly. We, specifically, study a conformally coupled scalar test field with a cubic interaction around these saddles. We find that the wave function coefficients can be written as discrete spectral sums with the summands containing the corresponding coefficients in the Einstein static universe, which are obtainable in analogy with the polytopes program for flat spacetime. Whereas the wave function coefficients of the flat FLRW case are given by integrals over shifted kinematics, the discrete spectrum on the three-sphere for Hartle-Hawking saddles produces sums. We identify the coefficients, which depend on the final hypersurface through a phase fixed by its size, with Srivastava-Daoust multi-variable hypergeometric functions. They satisfy recursion relations for any number of sites, under which the sums collapse into rational functions. For the one- and two-site Feynman-Witten tree diagrams, we derive difference equations in the kinematic variables which close on a finite set of sums, giving a discrete kinematic flow. The transformation matrices are upper triangular with rational elements, and satisfy a consistency condition which makes the flow path independent. We then obtain the two-, three- and four-point cosmological correlators. At the late-time conformal boundary, we derive an explicit difference equation for the four-point function.
authors: Vikramaditya Mondal, Shinji Mukohyama

papers.title: Cosmological Dressing Rules for Massive Scalars
papers.abstract: The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation of de Sitter correlation functions comes in different guises including harmonic analysis and dressed flat space correlators. We observe that these are equivalent spectral representations of the same Sturm-Liouville problem. Starting from the latter we derive dressing rules for scalar fields of arbitrary mass with auxiliary propagators in the form of Euler integrals that are accessible to flat space diagrammatic tools.
authors: Jonathan Gr\"afe, Matthias Nowinski, Ivo Sachs, Siva Pawan Venna

papers.title: Revealing Bell Nonlocality Does Not Require the Same Physical Measurement to be Performed Twice
papers.abstract: Bell inequality violations, or Bell nonlocality for short, is not only central to testing the foundations of quantum physics but have also become an essential ingredient of numerous quantum information protocols, from quantum key distribution to the device-independent certification of randomness and secure communication. Existing analyses of Bell nonlocality assume that a small set of predefined measurement directions can be reproduced exactly. But what if these directions cannot be reproduced at all? This may happen for fundamental or technical reasons, such as variations in the measurement apparatus. Here we show that the violation of a Bell inequality remains possible and that it also retains its operational significance, even when the measurement directions never repeat. We experimentally confirm these results using polarization-entangled photons, detecting only one particle pair per randomly chosen analyzer direction. Our results establish the robustness of Bell inequality violations against imperfect measurement repeatability and further connect Bell tests with the broader framework of randomized measurements. Moreover, they extend quantum information protocols to settings with limited measurement control, including quantum device certification, communication complexity, and quantum cryptography.
authors: Pawe{\l} Cie\'sli\'nski, Carlotta Versmold, Jan W\'ojcik, Eun Mi Kim, Jan Dziewior, Pawe{\l} Kurzy\'nski, Tomasz Paterek, Harald Weinfurter, Wies{\l}aw Laskowski

papers.title: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
papers.abstract: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.
authors: Narmin Nasibova, Francesco Giacosa

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.
authors: Alireza Allahyari, Shinji Mukohyama, Yi Pang

papers.title: Subsystem Flow: Quantum Error Correction, Petz Recovery, and Ergodic Inclusions
papers.abstract: In quantum error correction (QEC), the goal is to engineer an encoding that protects logical information against the erasure of a physical subsystem. In local many-body quantum systems, by contrast, nature provides a subsystem inclusion $\mN\subset \mM$ in a fixed reference state $\ket{\Omega}$. Asking whether the inclusion admits a reference-preserving code that protects subsystem $\mN$ against erasure of the complement is equivalent to asking whether $\mN$ is preserved under the modular dynamics of $\mM$ in this state (modular autonomy). We define the subsystem flow, which measures the departure from this error correction regime. Away from autonomy, the infinitesimal flow quantifies relative-entropy loss, while the history algebra and persistent core describe which observables the modular orbit generates and retains. We call an inclusion ergodic when modular orbits generate everything and retain nothing. Analytic continuation of subsystem flow yields Petz recovery maps and a family of positive inclusion parent Hamiltonians. We show that, in general, evolving with these parent Hamiltonians allows $\mN$ to leave $\mM$, and in some cases, it can generate the entire $\mM\vee\mM'$. Inclusions with a common cyclic and separating vector generate everything, and standard inclusions of factors, such as those of nested subregions in QFT, are ergodic. Moreover, the $L^2$-nuclearity property implies that the spectrum of parent Hamiltonians is discrete. We define a dissipative semigroup by repeating the Petz recovery map, whose fixed-point algebra is the modular persistent core and whose spectrum is gapped under the assumption of $L^2$-nuclearity. We conjecture that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of inclusion parent Hamiltonians can be used to define local spectral measures of quantum chaos.
authors: Yidong Chen, Nima Lashkari, Kwing Lam Leung

papers.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
papers.abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.
authors: Shiyong Guo, Enrico Rinaldi, Jad C. Halimeh, Brian Swingle

papers.title: Superradiant photon bunching in nanolasers: from a polarization-order hierarchy of the master equation to Dicke Markov chains
papers.abstract: In nanolasers, a few to a few hundred quantum emitters share a single mode of light. Coupled identically to the mode, the emitters do not radiate independently but form collective bright and dark states, producing superradiant bursts and strongly bunched photon statistics below the laser threshold. We investigate to what extent this behavior can be understood as random jumps between collective Dicke states. From the laser master equation, we derive a hierarchy of models defined by the polarization order, i.e., the number of photons involved in the coherence between the emitters and the light, and include the coherence to various orders. With all of the coherences eliminated, we obtain a Dicke Markov chain, a stochastic jump process over the photon number and the Dicke states, in which collective effects enter only through enhanced or suppressed transition rates. It predicts superthermal bunching and a strong even--odd dependence on the emitter number. It recovers about 80\% of the bunching in the most coherent regime, where conventional rate equations predict no superthermal bunching. Keeping the first polarization order, i.e., the optical polarization, and eliminating the second order, i.e., the two-photon coherences, yields a population-polarization model, which recovers the bunching of the full master equation almost perfectly. This hierarchy of polarization orders is an alternative to the cumulant expansion and, unlike it, recovers the master equation at the highest order. As a numerically exact reference, a symmetry-reduced master equation extends the simulation range all the way to 34 (24) emitters below (above) threshold. The Dicke Markov chain can be solved directly for hundreds of emitters and sampled for thousands of emitters, further extending the range of numerical methods. We compare the numerical performance of the methods in detail to guide the choice of technique.
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Jesper M{\o}rk

papers.title: Exact Infrared Triangle in Gravity with Long-Range Interactions
papers.abstract: Einstein gravity coupled to massless matter exhibits universality in the infrared. In the presence of long-range interactions we show that a novel superrotation charge conservation is equivalent to the massless limit of the classical logarithmic soft graviton theorem, and we propose a formula for the corresponding tail to the displacement memory. These results, which extend earlier work on gravity coupled to massive matter in a qualitatively different way, are exact in the gravitational coupling and reveal that long-range gravitational dressings resum. We also compute higher-order corrections to the known superrotation charge which are exact in the gravitational coupling and would correspond to a 1-loop exact correction to the Cachazo-Strominger subleading soft graviton theorem.
authors: Sangmin Choi, Ameya Kadhe, Prahar Mitra, Andrea Puhm

papers.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
papers.abstract: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, N\'eel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.
authors: Alessandro Mariani

papers.title: Eigenvalue Crossings and Discontinuous BBP Transitions in Spiked Euclidean Random Matrices
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a rank-one signal embedded in a symmetric Euclidean random matrix, whose dense and geometrically correlated entries generally lack rotational invariance. We show that signal recovery through the leading eigenvector is governed by a competition between the principal directions of the noise and the signal. In particular, the signal may already be encoded in a subleading eigendirection, while remaining undetected by the leading principal component. As the signal strength increases, a crossing between competing eigenvalues can change their ordering, causing the leading eigenvector to switch abruptly from a noise-dominated to a signal-bearing direction. This mechanism gives rise to a discontinuous BBP-type transition, in which the overlap with the signal jumps from zero to a finite value. Using the replica method, we reduce the problem to a Fredholm eigenvalue equation and derive general criteria for the existence of a positive recovery threshold, expressed in terms of the unperturbed spectral edge, the spike mean and the spatial averages of the principal eigenfunctions. We obtain analytically the limiting largest eigenvalue, eigenvector-component distribution and signal overlap, and illustrate the results with explicit solutions for quadratic distance and rank-two kernels, finding excellent agreement with numerical diagonalisation.
authors: Pasquale Casaburi, Pierpaolo Vivo

papers.title: Magnetic-slope crossovers in the QCD bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio
papers.abstract: How a magnetic field alters dissipation in quark--gluon matter is almost unconstrained from first principles, since real-time transport is not directly accessible to lattice simulation. Using a top-down MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction of a QCD-like thermal plasma, together with a kinetic-theory identity within a specified single-mode quasiparticle truncation and a compatibility construction using available lattice equation-of-state data, we propose a normalization-insensitive sign prediction that the field slope of the longitudinal bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio \zeta_\parallel/\eta_\parallel reverses sign twice with temperature---below and above the deconfinement pseudo-critical temperature T_0, at T_1<T_0<T_2 (the lower reversal T_1 conditional on a stated pion-gas rate inequality). A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available \zeta_\parallel/s, \eta_\parallel/s plots.
authors: Aalok Misra, Shivam S. Kushwah, Keshav Dasgupta, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon

papers.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
papers.abstract: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.
authors: Joydeep Chakravarty

papers.title: Extension of Poincare superalgebra via hidden symmetries
papers.abstract: Isometries of a manifold and special types of spinors called Killing spinors which are related to Killing vector fields constitute a symmetry superalgebra structure corresponding to Poincare superalgebra. The antisymmetric generalization of Killing vector fields to higher degree forms which are called Killing-Yano forms are considered. The odd part of the Poincare superalgebra is extended from the space of Killing vector fields and their rotational representation to the space of special odd Killing-Yano forms and special even closed conformal Killing-Yano forms. The even part is again corresponds to the space of Killing spinors. By defining the relevant brackets, we show that hidden symmetries and Killing spinors together define an extension of the Poincare superalgebra.
authors: \"{U}mit Ertem

papers.title: Quasi-Cyclic Qudit Lifted Product Codes with Almost Linear Minimum Distance
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computation with low overhead, and qudits offer advantages over qubits including more efficient information representation, improved magic state distillation, and richer algebraic structure for code design. Asymptotically good QLDPC codes arise from the lifted product (LP) construction with non-abelian lifts, but cyclic lifts remain attractive in practice because the resulting quasi-cyclic codes have circulant structure that hardware decoders exploit, which matters especially for non-binary decoders with costly check node operations. We introduce a qudit generalization of the LP construction over cyclic group algebras, which extends hypergraph product and LP codes to arbitrary prime-power dimensions and yields quasi-cyclic qudit CSS codes for every stacking order. We bound encoding rates via a connection to additive codes, and show that in the fully stacked case, qudit LP codes built from lifted Tanner codes on expander graphs form families with $\Theta(\log N)$ logical qudits and almost linear minimum distance $\Theta(N/\log N)$, via a distance bound that holds for a general class of LP factors. We also study an additive decoder for general qudit codes and a linear merged-syndrome decoder for fully stacked codes. Monte Carlo simulations under a depolarizing channel with equal symbol error probability show that qudit codes achieve lower frame error rates than comparable qubit codes, and that the linear decoder gives further gains for fully stacked codes.
authors: Shantom K. Borah, Abhinav Vaishya, V. Lalitha, Asit Kumar Pradhan, Bane Vasic, Narayanan Rengaswamy

papers.title: Comprehensive quantum electrodynamics of fast electrons interacting with dissipative nanostructures and quantum light
papers.abstract: Theoretical descriptions of the quantum electrodynamical interaction between fast electrons and nanostructures conventionally rely on standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED), which, when applied to bounded objects in vacuum, formally requires an asymptotic limiting procedure to account for free-space radiation modes. To explicitly incorporate these modes from the outset, we employ the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF), which independently quantizes both the asymptotic scattering modes and the electromagnetic field generated by dissipative material sources. Utilizing an exact second-order Magnus expansion, we derive a closed-form, nonperturbative master formula for the transverse-momentum-resolved energy exchange probability. In the unilluminated regime, we demonstrate that at finite nanostructure temperatures, the vacuum scattering and thermal material fluctuations do not mathematically recombine into the total imaginary part of the dyadic Green's function. This breakdown does not violate the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem, because the explicit zero-temperature scattering field acts as an independent dynamical system that maintains the configuration out of global thermodynamic equilibrium. This fundamental separation reveals an intrinsic Stokes--Anti-Stokes asymmetry, yielding distinct transverse diffraction patterns for energy loss and thermal energy gain, and establishing a generalized detailed-balance relation that governs the radiative reduction of the apparent temperature in nanoscale electron thermometry. In the illuminated regime, our framework rigorously incorporates quantum-optical states into macroscopic dissipative electrodynamics, demonstrating that...
authors: Alessandro Ciattoni

papers.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function
papers.abstract: By utilizing the derivation of quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bound and an argument put forward by Efimov and Dodonov, we derive several uncertainty relations for mixed states that constrain the diagonal product, trace, and each diagonal element of the covariance matrix of multiple observables. By choosing the observables to be the symmetric logarithmic derivative, the uncertainty relations imply various geometric bounds on quantum Fisher information matrix caused by mean Uhlmann curvature, which in pure states become geometric bounds on quantum metric caused by Berry curvature. Our formalism reveals optical sum rules for velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and how they are bounded by the Berry curvature and commutator of velocity operators. Canonical ensembles of spins, topological materials, common semiconductors, and transition metal dichalcogenides are used to verify these geometric bounds and uncertainty relations.
authors: Felipe P. Abreu, Luis F. C\'{a}rdenas-Castillo, David Porlles, Wei Chen

papers.title: Self-Force and Bremsstrahlung in Finite Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the self-force and the accompanying Bremsstrahlung for a moving point charge in nonlinear electrodynamics with finite self-field and self-energy. The self-force in the Maxwell theory has been the subject of many studies, often by renowned physicists. After reviewing Coleman's lucid treatise for Maxwell among them, we wish to explore the same question in the Born--Infeld theory, our prototype. We independently compute the local self-force and the global radiative dissipation, and show how the two are mutually consistent. Despite the nonlinearity turning off for the asymptotic radiative field, its residual effect survives via the effective multipole moments of a moving charge, allowing deviation from Maxwell. We close with a detailed discussion about two different manifestations of the self-force in the literature and how these enter our computation. One of the appendices explores Born--Infeld ModMax as a generalization.
authors: Kyungsun Lee, Piljin Yi

papers.title: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups
papers.abstract: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. Yet, in contrast to Bell scenarios or prepare-measure scenarios with shared randomness, no general method is known to separate classical and quantum statistics. Here we close this gap by deriving dimensional inequalities to separate classical and quantum statistics in CS. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness. The inequalities also yield a dimension witness for both correlated and anti-correlated statistics, without the need of measurement incompatibility.
authors: Albert Rico, Javier Fern\'andez, Mani Zartab, John Calsamiglia, Some Sankar Bhattacharya

papers.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
papers.abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.
authors: Hudaiba Soomro, Talise Oh, M. A. Eriksson, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen

papers.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.
authors: Jiang Yuhan, Matthew Otten

papers.title: Fr\'echet structure over AF algebras I: The compact case
papers.abstract: This is the first of two papers devoted to spatial Fr\'echet structures on AF algebras and their derivations. Here, we study the simplest example of such a structure: the Fr\'echet algebra of almost-local compact operators associated with a fixed orthonormal basis. We revisit the characterization of its continuous derivations in terms of infinite matrices and their operator-theoretic implementation on rapidly decreasing vectors. Reformulating this description in the language of 0-chains, borrowed from the theory of quantum many-body systems, we establish a sufficient condition for continuity in terms of spatial growth. Finally, we construct a Fr\'echet-continuous symmetric derivation that does not generate a one-parameter group of automorphisms of this algebra that is strongly continuous with respect to its Fr\'echet topology.
authors: Giuseppe De Nittis, Juli\'an G\'omez

papers.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
papers.abstract: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.
authors: Shuntaro Aoki, Zhehan Qin, Masahide Yamaguchi, Yuhang Zhu

papers.title: Anti-periodic Gravitino and Dirac Effective Operators
papers.abstract: Introducing a preserved $U(1)_R$ symmetry forbids gravitini Majorana masses while allowing a Dirac mass. We investigate how a Dirac mass for gravitini can be described by an effective operator in $N=1$ superspace, in analogy with the well-known Dirac gaugino mass. We find that the corresponding spin-$3/2$ bilinear operator can be expressed in terms of gauge-invariant gravitino curvature superfields coupled through a nonlocal kernel involving an inverse d'Alembertian. We study this construction in minimal five-dimensional supergravity compactified on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$. The gravitino satisfies anti-periodic boundary conditions induced by a Scherk-Schwarz twist. The physical Kaluza-Klein Dirac masses then appear as poles in the two-point functions of the curvature superfields associated with sources localized at the endpoints. Separation of physical and gauge modes relates these propagators to a quadratic fermionic kernel represented by a $16\times16$ matrix. Its elements match the fermionic components of two invariants written in $N=1$ superspace, including their spinor contractions and normalization. This matching is carried out on a fixed background with a nonzero radion auxiliary field.
authors: Karim Benakli

papers.title: Operator uncertainty and cross-domain information in quantum signals: Second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design
papers.abstract: We derive second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design by combining entropic uncertainty relations with the covariance description of continuous-variable systems. For any state with finite second moments and entropies, the mutual information between the arrival time and the transverse wave number, which are compatible observables from different canonical pairs, is bounded above by the logarithm of twice the smaller of the time-frequency and position-wave-number uncertainty products. We demonstrate that a Gaussian wave packet with a bilinear space-time phase saturates this bound for every admissible set of standard-deviation budgets, and that the bound therefore provides a necessary and sufficient condition for reaching a target information within the canonical model. For this state, the joint measurement of the arrival time and the transverse wave number is optimal among local Gaussian measurements, yields the R\'enyi-2 entropy of the reduced state, and attains the quantum Fisher information for the coupling at fixed input widths. We also show that, with additive detector noise, timing jitter limits the recorded information to a level set by the ratio of jitter to pulse duration. These results provide a framework for designing spatiotemporally coupled quantum signals, and we propose an optical realization based on pulse-front tilt and a lens.
authors: Mostafizur Rahaman Laskar, Sajad Daei, Gabor Fodor, Mikael Skoglund, Franco Nori

papers.title: Entropy production decomposition and fluctuation theorems under continuous feedback: From prescribed to stochastic protocols
papers.abstract: When a system is driven by a prescribed protocol, the entropy production can be decomposed into the housekeeping and non-autonomous contributions, each satisfying a fluctuation theorem. Under feedback control, however, the feedback parameter depends on measurement outcomes rather than following a prescribed protocol. To study how the decomposition changes, we consider an overdamped Brownian particle at position $x$ with a low-pass-filtered measurement signal $D$ as the feedback parameter. Regarding each realization of $D$ as a stochastic protocol, we derive fluctuation theorems for the entropy production associated with the dynamics of $x$ and of $D$, and interpret them in terms of the information flow. For a solvable harmonic model, we map the dynamics onto an autonomous system in which the measurement and filtering process acts as an effective thermal bath. Feedback cooling thus corresponds to heat conduction from the physical bath through the particle to this colder bath, and the information flow can be interpreted as the entropy associated with the heat conduction between $x$ and $D$. We verify these results by numerical simulations.
authors: Long Him Cheung

papers.title: Mapping the High-Field Response of Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors
papers.abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are increasingly being integrated into cryogenic quantum-sensing platforms that operate in large magnetic fields. Here, the high-field limits of these measurements were probed by characterizing the dark count response of a NbTiN SNSPD at up to 14~T using in situ control of the detector orientation and benchmarking that performance against normal detector operation in smaller magnetic fields. The detector performance is strongly anisotropic: perpendicular magnetic fields rapidly reduce the usable bias-current range, whereas near-parallel alignment enables operation at substantially larger total fields, with a finite operating margin retained to 12~T and measurable dark-count response at the 14~T field limit. The angular dependence is governed predominantly by the perpendicular component of the magnetic field, consistent with vortex-mediated suppression of the superconducting current scale. The same field-dependent current scale also determines the electrical pulse amplitude, linking high-field detector operation directly to readout performance. These results establish a practical route for deploying SNSPDs in multi-tesla quantum-sensing and high-field cryogenic experiments.
authors: Harshit Agarwal, Yueh-Chun Wu, Katyayani Seal, Niels Noordzij, Andreas Fognini, Ronan Gourgues, G\'abor B. Hal\'asz, Benjamin J. Lawrie, Nirjhar Sarkar

papers.title: Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $\epsilon=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=\alpha^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.
authors: Soner Albayrak

papers.title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.
authors: Niloy Deb Roy Mishu, Lei Jiang, Mohsen Heidari, Ruizhe Zhang, Fan Chen

papers.title: Critical behavior of the bosonized Schwinger model with uniform matrix product states
papers.abstract: Quantum electrodynamics in two spacetime dimensions, also known as the Schwinger model, admits a dual formulation in terms of a non-compact boson field. Using a Hamiltonian lattice discretization of the bosonized model, we compute the critical mass of the continuum Schwinger model at $\theta=\pi$. We numerically obtain the ground state on an infinite chain by the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm, preserving charge conjugation exactly. As a truncated basis for the local Hilbert space, we employ the oscillator basis that diagonalizes the one-site reduced density matrix of the free limit. We constrain the fitting functions for the continuum extrapolation using the Symanzik effective theory for lattice corrections. Our result for the critical mass, $(m/g)_c = 0.333\,555(5)$, agrees with recent staggered-fermion determinations at comparable precision.
authors: Takuya Okuda

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models.
